gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ his argument that nobody objected.
gaps.explanation: So + adjective at the front: was his argument that…

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ a debut film attracted such wide attention.
gaps.explanation: 'Rarely has a debut film attracted …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
gaps.explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we started ___ the engine failed.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair: Hardly had we started when…

gaps.sentence: So ferocious ___ the storm prove that three coastal villages were evacuated.
gaps.explanation: With the bare verb 'prove', the inversion takes do-support: did the storm prove.
